chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Qalānisī, from Aḥmad ibn al-Faḍl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Fazarah, from Anas or Haytham ibn al-Barāʾ, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: “A thief enters my house seeking my life and my property.” So he said: “Kill him, and make Allah and whoever heard bear witness that his blood is upon my neck.”

key_terms.اقْتُلْهُ: kill him; an authorization to use lethal force in this situation
key_terms.اللِّصُّ: the thief; the aggressor who unlawfully enters
key_terms.بَيْتِي: my house; the protected private dwelling
key_terms.دَمَهُ: his blood; meaning liability for his killing
key_terms.فِي عُنُقِي: upon my neck; an expression of assumed responsibility
key_terms.مَالِي: my property; one’s wealth or possessions
key_terms.نَفْسِي: my life; one’s person or self

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام say about killing a thief who enters one’s house seeking life and property?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a thief who enters a person’s home intending to attack his life and seize his property. It indicates permission to defend oneself in such a case, with the Imam عليه السلام explicitly assuming responsibility for the ruling.
